payload.headline: Meta at 609.89 stalls below resistance; wait for the 2027-01-27 report

summary.thesis: Sales are still growing fast, but margins and free cash flow have fallen, and the price already assumes cash-flow growth stronger than anything in the data.
summary.decision: Long-term wait and swing no trade until the price falls to the support and value levels or the 2027-01-27 report shows cash flow recovering.
summary.act_at: Buy at 475.85; swing only after a close above 626.86

payload.happening: Meta rose 3.4% to 609.89. That put it just under a resistance zone from 611.95 to 626.54, a price band where rallies have stalled before. The stock is still in a downtrend, below its 50-day average of 672.4 and its 200-day average of 626.86. No news has come in since the last note. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand looks solid. Sales grew 27.53% over the last twelve months, to 241.6B from 189.5B. Growth is slowing, though: sales grew 26.07% year over year last quarter, down from 33.08% two quarters ago. Profitability is the real problem. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 28.6B from 44.8B. R&D takes 31.68% of revenue. The company now holds slightly more debt than cash (net cash -1.2B, total debt 83.7B), but it has 82.4B of liquidity, so funding is not the risk. The filings data also says the company missed forecasts last quarter by 29% and that profit per share is lagging sales. The mix of rising spending and shrinking cash flow fits a heavy investment cycle (general knowledge), but the reports do not yet show that spending paying off. Two items affect only sentiment and governance, not the business: insiders sold $14.1M outside pre-set plans, and the tech market is in a downtrend with elevated fear. At risk: margins and cash generation. Not at risk: demand, the 81.03% gross margin, and the ability to pay debts.

worth.text: The methods disagree a lot. The discounted cash flow model (DCF), which values the company on its future cash, starts from today's reduced free cash flow of 28.6B and gives 244.22 (bear), 379.4 (base) and 517.42 (bull). All three are below the 609.89 price. To justify 609.89, cash flow would need to start growing at 36.7% a year. That is above the fastest growth figure the model uses as a starting point, last year's 28% sales growth. Even at 30% starting growth the model gives 477.73. The other method compares the price with Meta's own past price-to-sales ratios and gives a much higher range: 475.85 at the low end, 707.21 in the middle and 881.21 at the high end. At 6.5 times sales, the stock is at the 37th percentile of its own 5-year range and close to the peer median of 6.0. Its trailing P/E, the price divided by the last year's earnings per share, is 20.9. The gap between the methods comes down to one thing: whether 28.6B is the new normal for free cash flow or a low point in a spending cycle. If margins slip further, to a 24% operating margin, the DCF value drops to 245.02. My range runs from the low end of the sales history to its middle.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the heavy spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales grew 27.53% over the last twelve months, to 241.6B, so demand is not the problem.
At 6.5 times sales the stock is at only the 37th percentile of its own 5-year history, and the middle of that history is worth 707.21.
A gross margin of 81.03% shows the core product is still very profitable before the investment spending.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and the price needs it to start growing at 36.7% a year to make sense.
Operating margin fell to 32.86% from 43.23%, and at a 24% margin the DCF value would be just 245.02.
The trend is down, with the price below the 50-day average of 672.4 and a committee call of Reduce.

levels.what: Bottom of the lower support zone (576.61–591.58). A close below it would mean the downtrend has resumed after today's bounce.
The DCF bull value. Below it, the price no longer sits above every cash-flow estimate.
Buy level: the low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 477.73 value at 30% growth, so a buy here does not depend on a full margin recovery.

longterm.why: At 609.89 the price is above every DCF value, the business is graded C, and free cash flow is shrinking. Buying now means paying in advance for a recovery the reports have not shown yet.

swing.why: The bounce stopped just under the 611.95–626.54 resistance zone. The falling 20-day average (615.27) and the 200-day average (626.86) sit just above, and the average daily move (ATR) of 25.36 is about the width of that zone. No trade until a close above 626.86.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.5% move by Dec 18 and an 18.3% move by Feb 19, a window that includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report settles the cash-flow question, so there is no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows free cash flow rising back toward 44.8B and operating margin moving back toward 43.23%. That would support the upper half of the 475.85–707.21 range and justify moving to buy.
A close above 626.86, the 200-day average and the top of the first resistance zone, would break the downtrend's pattern of lower highs and open a swing entry.
Another drop in operating margin toward 24% would cut the cash-flow value to 245.02. In that case the 475.85 buy level would no longer hold, and the long-term action would move to avoid.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait and no trade, because the 609.89 close stayed below the 611.95–626.54 resistance zone and free cash flow is still 28.6B against 44.8B a year earlier.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
